note: Devi Bhagavata, Skandha 5, 6: Hindi put back on the verse it belongs to, matched by Sanskrit content and the printed numbering. The Hindi is the printed Gita Press translation with mechanical clean-up only; where the edition groups verses, the paragraph is shown once on the first verse (hindiRange) and the others point to it (hindiSeeVerse). Every entry is in data/ocr-hindi-review.json under this queue and is withheld until proofread against the printed page.

guards: Sanskrit 3-gram Jaccard >= 0.6 and >= 0.15 above the next printed verse
printed adhyaya (between two consecutive Sanskrit colophons; skandha named in the colophon or the running heads) agrees with the verse
printed Sanskrit verse number agrees with the verse
the Hindi paragraph is printed beside it, closes with its own "॥ n ॥", its printed number covers the verse, and the paragraph before it ends exactly on the verse before (no half verses)
a range covers at most 5 verses, every one passes the Sanskrit and number guards, and they are consecutive in the library
the library verse holds a single printed verse
no line of the paragraph was dropped or left unclassified as unreadable, and it does not open with a stray letter
no page number, running head, colophon or heading left after mechanical clean-up (ASCII digits, page specks, avagraha and visarga glyphs)
a single: the Hindi shares at least 2 more word stems with its own verse than with any verse 1-3 places away; a range: at least 3 stems and 2 more than the neighbouring range of the same length
